resources.string: Forkcast lives in a private GitHub repository. The link opens it in your browser (sign in to GitHub to see it).
Waiting for Android to install it. Confirm when asked; your data stays.
Android needs your OK once before Forkcast can install its own updates: turn on \"Allow from this source\", then come back and tap Install.
The repository is private, so checking from the app needs a GitHub token (below). You can also open Releases on GitHub and download the APK there.
No connection. Try again when you\'re online.
GitHub refused the token. Check that it hasn\'t expired and can read the forkcast repository (Contents: read-only).
GitHub has no release yet, or the token can\'t see the repository.
GitHub sent something other than the APK. Try again; if it keeps happening, get the APK from the Releases page.
GitHub answered with an error (HTTP %1$d). Try again later.
That release has no APK attached.
The download isn\'t a valid APK. Try again.
The download is signed with a different key, so Android couldn\'t install it over this app. Nothing was changed.
This phone already has a newer build (%1$d) than that release (%2$d). Nothing was changed.
The install didn\'t finish. Nothing was changed.
The install didn\'t finish: %1$s. Nothing was changed.

1. On github.com, open Settings › Developer settings › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens › Generate new token.
2. Repository access: Only select repositories › forkcast.
3. Permissions › Repository permissions › Contents: Read-only.
4. Pick an expiration, generate, copy the token, and paste it here.

It stays encrypted on this phone and is only sent to GitHub when you tap Check for updates.
